summary: Today’s pulse tracks Andy Burnham’s plan to scrap technology department triggers backlash, Cuba edges toward breakdown as power cuts and US meddling push society to brink, and Russian online retail warehouses hit by deadly Ukrainian strikes. Across Guardian, BBC, and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are department, technology, and backlash. In the background, Why is it so hard for the U.S. to win wars and Opinion: The continued courage of Captain Sully keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Andy Burnham’s plan to scrap technology department triggers backlash
headlines.description: MPs and industry experts say potential reorganisation will waste time at critical moment for AI and economic growth Andy Burnham’s plan to scrap the government’s technology department has triggered an angry backlash from MPs, Whitehall officials and tech experts. The incoming prime minister has asked officials to draw up plans to abolish the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology as part of a wider Whitehall shake-up.

headlines.title: Cuba edges toward breakdown as power cuts and US meddling push society to brink
headlines.description: As Cuba swelters under six-month oil blockade imposed by US, tempers are fraying and unrest is growing When Cuba’s national grid collapses, as it did for the third time in 10 days on Tuesday, a collective groan spreads across its cities and people wonder, again, whether the island’s antiquated electricity system may soon become unrecoverable. The 777-mile Caribbean island of 9.5 million people has been sweltering under a six-month-long oil blockade imposed by the US, part of a pressure campaign to bring down its communist government. But the parlous state of Cuba’s infrastructure goes far further back.

headlines.title: Russian online retail warehouses hit by deadly Ukrainian strikes
headlines.description: Drones targeted Wildberries facilities near Moscow and in Tambov. Ukraine's leader called them "major logistics facilities" supplying "sanctioned components".

headlines.title: Why is it so hard for the U.S. to win wars?
headlines.description: U.S. presidents have promised short, decisive wars in Afghanistan, Iraq and Iran. All have proved much more difficult than advertised and fallen far short of the political goals set at the beginning.

headlines.title: Opinion: The continued courage of Captain Sully
headlines.description: Retired pilot Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger is known for safely landing an airplane on the Hudson River in 2009. This week, he announced that he has Alzheimer's disease.

headlines.title: US strikes hit Iran for seventh consecutive night
headlines.description: Iran has retaliated against US allies in the region, with Kuwait reporting that a power and water plant had been hit.

headlinePool.title: What will Keir Starmer do next?
headlinePool.description: Outgoing PM has joked about cookery classes and cutting hedges, but does the international stage beckon? As his time in Downing Street comes to an end, Keir Starmer has been joking with friends about what he might do after he stands down as prime minister. He has teased that he might take a cookery course. “He needs it, he only makes two meals,” one friend said. Another not entirely serious suggestion was cutting his father-in-law’s hedge in the expectation that if he did well, he could graduate to lawns.

headlinePool.title: White House backs Argentina players over Falklands banner in World Cup semi-final
headlinePool.description: White House Fifa taskforce chief defends Argentina footballers, saying US believes in free speech The White House has backed Argentina’s footballers who displayed a banner supporting their country’s claim to the Falklands Islands after their World Cup semi-final victory against England. After Argentina’s 2-1 win in a fractious match in Atlanta on Wednesday, some players held up a banner that said: “ Las Malvinas son Argentinas ” – using the country’s term for the South Atlantic islands.

headlinePool.title: 8 killed and more than 60 wounded in Ukrainian drone attack on Russian regions
headlinePool.description: Kyiv's forces are continuing their aerial campaign against energy infrastructure and military targets inside Russia, aiming to undermine Moscow's war effort.

headlinePool.title: Andy Burnham considers radical shake-up to cut energy bills
headlinePool.description: Labour leader examining proposals to overhaul gas standing charges and make heat pumps cheaper to run than boilers Andy Burnham is considering radical plans that could cut household energy bills by £130 a year and make running a heat pump cheaper than a gas boiler. In his speech on Friday as he became the new Labour leader , Burnham promised to reduce the price of “essentials”, and a cost of living package is expected to be one of his first announcements in Downing Street.

headlinePool.title: The 2000s called. They want their digital camera back
headlinePool.description: Why are people who weren't born 25 years ago snapping up the digital camera of that era? Blame Taylor Swift, trend cycles, childhood nostalgia and smartphone fatigue.

headlinePool.title: Poultry sector growth plan risks UK national security, campaigners warn
headlinePool.description: Government’s food security push is said to rely on animal feed imports with vulnerability to supply chain shocks The government’s planned poultry sector growth plan is a risk to national security, campaigners have warned. Earlier this month, the environment secretary, Emma Reynolds , told the Groundswell agriculture festival that the key to improving food security was consuming more homegrown produce, and said this was why the government had set up the Farming and Food Partnership Board, whose members include industry leaders such as the president of the National Farmers’ Union and the chief executive of the Food & Drink Federation.

headlinePool.title: Arizona teen hailed for helping save woman with dementia wandering in 103F heat
headlinePool.description: Fire crew in Gilbert to honor Royal Cothrun, 14, for helping elderly woman who became disoriented amid heatwave An Arizona fire department is formally honoring a 14-year-old boy who recently helped save an elderly woman with dementia after she wandered miles off course amid potentially lethal temperatures, saying the teenager demonstrated “heroism … quick thinking and compassion”. Royal Cothrun was riding his bicycle in June in the town of Gilbert when he encountered Theresa Morgan as she struggled to walk through 103F (39.4C) heat with a grocery bag dangling off one arm and a purse on the other, according to authorities as well as reporting by the local news outlet KNXV .
